questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles duplicate events? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why is the dedup key the eventId from the payload rather than the Kafka topic-partition-offset?
choices: Offsets are only unique within a consumer group, so two groups would collide.
UUIDs are faster to index than a long offset.
The producer may publish the same logical event twice (for example on a retry), and each copy gets a different offset but carries the same eventId.
Kafka reuses offsets after log compaction.

questions.prompt: Two instances of the service receive the same event at the same time, for example after a rebalance. What ensures at most one of them runs reserve for it?
choices: The primary key on (event_id, consumer) together with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING: only one insert reports 1 row inserted, the other reports 0.
The Kafka consumer group guarantees a record is never delivered to two instances.
The UPDATE ... WHERE available >= ? in reserve fails for the second instance.
The DefaultErrorHandler serializes handling across instances.

questions.prompt: The process crashes right after inventory.reserve commits but before ack.acknowledge() is called. What happens when the record is redelivered?
choices: Stock is reserved a second time.
The event is recognised as already processed, acknowledged, and not reserved again, leaving exactly one reservation.
The record is sent to a dead-letter topic.
The listener throws because the reservation row already exists.
